skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders - support and host discussions within a multidisciplinary team, with potentially difficult dynamics - be an advocate for the team externally - manage differing stakeholder perspectives
You can: - undertake data profiling and source system analysis - present clear insights to colleagues to support the end use of the data

You can: - experiment with unfamiliar and emerging technologies, or familiar technologies in new data contexts, with guidance - share what you learn with the team, explaining potential benefits, risks, and practical considerations - identify opportunities to apply technology to improve data processes or outcomes in an operational setting or the wider organisation

You can: - build and review complex data models, ensuring adherence to standards - use data integration tools and languages to integrate and store data, and advise teams on best practice - ensure data for analysis meets data quality standards and is interoperable with other data sets, enabling reuse - work with other data professionals to improve modelling and integration patterns and standards

You can: - design an appropriate metadata repository - suggest changes to improve current metadata repositories - understand a range of tools for storing and working with metadata - advise less experienced members of the team about metadata management

You can: - initiate and monitor actions to investigate patterns and trends to resolve problems - effectively consult specialists where required - determine the appropriate resolution and assist with its implementation - determine preventative measures

skill: Programming and build (data and analytics engineering)
expected_level_description: You can: - lead the design, code, testing and deployment of secure, resilient and maintainable solutions - continuously improve the codebase and reliability of solutions - create automation to improve the software development life cycle - work with others to implement standards and good practice to ensure security, testability and maintainability of solutions
You can: - review requirements and specifications, and define test conditions - identify issues and risks associated with work - analyse and report test activities and results

skill: Turning business problems into data design
expected_level_description: You can: - design data architecture that deals with problems spanning different business areas - identify links between problems to devise common solutions - work across multiple subject areas, or a single large or complicated subject area - produce appropriate patterns

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - define data quality rules and measures - work with data providers to fix the root causes of poor quality

You can: - design data models and reference sets using clinical terminologies - map between terminologies and classifications, and explain the limits of a mapping - advise teams on terminology use in products and analytics
You can: - work with pseudonymised data and apply disclosure checks before releasing outputs - recognise when linked or detailed data could identify a patient
